selected.title: Markets bet 95pc chance of September rate hike after latest RBA comments
selected.summary: If you are struggling with current interest rates, the Reserve Bank's leaders delivered the sobering message that they are only just getting back to a "more sensible level".
selected.why: Markets sharply pricing in a surprise September rate hike based on new RBA comments.
selected.fullText: RBA leaders warn that interest rates are just back to 'sensible level' - ABC News Skip to main content Skip to news navigation, settings and search Explore the ABC news iview listen Loading ABC News News Home RBA leaders warn that interest rates are just back to 'sensible level' Share Share article RBA leaders warn that interest rates are just back to 'sensible level' By business editor Michael Janda , business reporter Gareth Hutchens and business correspondent David Taylor Topic: Interest Rates Posted Fri 18 Sep 2026 at 2:31pm Fri 18 Sep 2026 at 2:31pm Fri 18 Sep 2026 at 2:31pm RBA governor Michele Bullock and three other senior officials appear before the Standing Committee on Economics on September 18. ( ABC News: Tobias Hunt ) In short: RBA deputy governor Andrew Hauser said, "We're probably rather closer now to a more sensible level of long-term global real interest rates than we were a year or two ago." More economists have joined financial markets in tipping a September rate hike, with the possibility of another in November. What's next? The RBA's Monetary Policy Board will meet on September 28-29 to determine the next move in the cash rate target. abc.net.au/news/rba-governor-talks-interest-rates-at-parliamentary-hearing/107167676 Link copied Share Share article Tell us about your experience. Economists believe that the Reserve Bank's senior officials have decided that interest rates need to be hiked in September, and they expect the RBA's board to rubber stamp an increase in the cash rate to 4.6 per cent. This view was already developing following public appearances by deputy governor Andrew Hauser on the ABC's 7.30 program last week and the bank's chief economist Sarah Hunter at two conferences over the past fortnight. "We think tactically November's a better choice but certainly the internal members of the board are making noises that they want to go," former RBA assistant governor and current Westpac chief economist Luci Ellis told ABC News yesterday. " You can see that they're trying to signal to the market that they want to raise rates. So September is a genuine possibility as well. " Loading... However, an appearance in front of the federal parliament today by RBA governor Michele Bullock, deputy governor Andrew Hauser, and assistant governors Sarah Hunter and Brad Jones has many economists firmly convinced the bank will hike at the end of its next two-day meeting on September 29.
